rows.A_note: Level 2 is met: EV-041 shows 14 of 14 clauses monitored in Q1 and Q2, and EV-042 shows every finding with an owner, a target date and dated closure where closed. Level 3 is not met because the measure is evidenced for one period only. Level 4 also fails: EV-045 automation has only one quarter of block data, and the EV-046 audit is the first with the next not until 2027, so neither has recurred.
rows.B_note: Automated enforcement and independent audit exist, but only one audit cycle; recurrence not evidenced.

rows.A_note: Level 2 is met: EV-060 covers retention, disposal and notification, and EV-061 shows both retirements since the procedure were handled under it with deletion certificates and notifications. The EV-062 register exists but lacks the level-3 measurement. Level 4 evidence (playbook revisions) is absent.
rows.B_note: Procedure, register, and completeness measure exist; no evidence of playbook revision or knowledge preservation.

rows.A_note: DFE is in-house, so it is out of scope. The 4 covered vendors are fully evidenced (EV-070, EV-072, EV-073), but the open QAP gap means coverage is not complete. No level-3 threshold-based review is named.
rows.B_note: Risk assessments and contract terms exist for 4 of 6 vendors; no evidence of metrics or threshold review.

rows.A_note: The curriculum (EV-090) and the competency rubric (EV-092) are strong and role-based. Under the coverage definition, open completion gaps and an untested refresher cycle keep the score at level 1. Level 3 targets are not named.
rows.B_note: Role-based training, competency assessment, and refresh cycle exist; no evidence of rates tracked/reported against targets.

rows.A_note: Meetings are met: EV-101 shows four quarterly meetings with minutes and quorum, and the charter is EV-100. The decisions-log gap is the deciding failure, so the score is level 1. EV-103 would support level 4 only after levels 2 and 3 are met.
rows.B_note: Charter, minutes, and decision log with owners and due dates exist; no measure of items decided reported.

rows.A_note: EV-130 and EV-131 show real activity, but they do not meet the level-2 coverage test. The survey has two data points and no stated targets or reporting body, so level 3 would also fail.
rows.B_note: Survey metrics tracked against targets (EV-133), but no evidence of interventions triggered by dips or repeated cycles.

rows.A_note: EV-141 gives a minuted monthly cadence (9 of 9) and EV-142 gives a bidirectional feedback-to-change log, so level 2 holds. The distinguishing level-3 artefact, a metrics report against targets, is absent. The 46 unanswered operator items are a recorded backlog and do not defeat level 2.
rows.B_note: Feedback metrics reviewed on cadence (EV-141), but no evidence of real-time/public transparency or repeated influence.

rows.A_note: Anchor 0 says informal individual contact is level 1, not level 0. EV-171 is exactly that: a personal-basis co-authorship with no agreement, no data-sharing record and no review.
rows.B_note: Pack explicitly states no academic partnership, agreement, or contact exists (EV-170).

rows.A_note: EV-640 gives a plan with options, owner and date for each of the 5 top risks, so level 2 holds. Quarterly status review exists, but status reporting is not the measure the level-3 anchor requires.
rows.B_note: Completion-versus-plan and residual-risk reduction metrics reviewed each cycle, but no evidence of effectiveness measurement or plan revision from results.

rows.A_note: Level 2 is met: EV-670 and EV-672 show a maintenance plan and quarterly value review for all six systems. The artefact separating level 3 from level 2 (metric, value, target, report to a named body) is not present, so the score stays at 2.
rows.B_note: Level 3 satisfied: value metrics tracked against business case and reviewed on cadence (quarterly reviews, decisions recorded). No evidence of predictive modelling or automated optimisation.

rows.A_note: Level 2 relies on EV-680 being an organisation-wide procedure with recovery and lessons-learned log, applied in two incidents (EV-681). Its scope is not stated per system, so coverage is inferred from its being a general procedure. The procedure changes in EV-682 do not replace the level 3 measures.
rows.B_note: Level 3 satisfied: emergent-risk detections, response times and lessons closed measured per cycle (recovery records, lessons learned, procedure changes). No evidence of predictive or automated response.

rows.A_note: Level 2 is supported by EV-731 (all 5 releases cite a finding) and the EV-730 backlog. EV-730 gives only counts (22 raised, 16 released), so open/closed status per finding is inferred from those counts. Throughput reporting in EV-732 is present, but the effect measure is incomplete, so level 3 is not reached.
rows.B_note: Level 3 satisfied: improvement throughput and measured effect per release tracked. No evidence of optimisation or external recognition.

rows.A_note: EV-742 would meet the level 3 measure on its own: time-to-notify metric, 24-hour target, value of 2 of 3 within target, quarterly report to the AI Steering Committee. Level 3 requires level 2 evidence, and that is not fully named, so the score is 1. This would move to 3 if owner/status and system coverage are evidenced.
rows.B_note: Level 3 satisfied: incident metrics (counts, time-to-notify, recurrence) reviewed on cadence. No evidence of incident-driven change or automated detection.

rows.A_note: EV-210 documents the competency requirements, but the per-project composition review covers only a subset. There are no composition-versus-requirement metrics for level 3.
rows.B_note: Level 2 satisfied: documented competency requirements and team composition reviewed against them. No metrics tracked or reported.

rows.A_note: EV-220 gives a dated, approved strategy tied to the mission, which meets level 1. An asserted cadence without minutes does not meet level 2. EV-222 shows KPIs tracked, but level 3 cannot be reached without level 2.
rows.B_note: Level 3 satisfied: strategic KPIs tracked and reported to board on cadence. No evidence of strategy revisions traceable to KPI movement.

rows.A_note: Level 2 is met by EV-240 (formal statement) and EV-241 (Board Audit & Risk Committee approval, 2026-01-22). The qualitative tolerances are treated as 'where feasible'. The EV-242 Q3 breach is dated 2026-05, which falls in Q2, so the report dating is inconsistent. Level 3 is not reached because coverage of each tolerance is incomplete.
rows.B_note: Level 3 is fully satisfied: formal, approved, quantified tolerances, exposures tracked and reported on cadence, breach escalated. Level 4 requires evidence of the framework being reviewed and a tolerance being re-set, not just escalated.

rows.A_note: EV-280 (methodology and limitations) and EV-281 (TEVV plan with dates and owners) meet level 2. The pack evidences VIC-2 only and does not address the other registered systems, so level 2 rests on that gap being outside this pack. EV-282 (external metrology review) is a level 4 element, but it cannot lift the score because level 3 fails. No revisions traceable to measured method failures are shown
rows.B_note: All level 4 clauses are fully satisfied: methodology, TEVV, limitations, independent review, and revision traceable to review comments.

rows.A_note: EV-310 (scope statement) and EV-311 (5 changes approved under the recorded process) meet level 2. EV-312 is close to level 3 but fails the MEASURE test. Level 4 needs automated detection that blocked a deployment; the 2026-06 drift was caught by a check and re-scoped, and no automation is evidenced.
rows.B_note: Scope-drift checks are measured per release and acted on, but no evidence of automated drift detection.

rows.A_note: A procedure (EV-330) and an override log (EV-331) exist, which meets level 1. Per-system coverage of the scope register is also not shown. Override and agreement rates per system are not reported for level 3; the 51 of 60 audit is a one-off sample. Only one assessment exists, so there is no cadence.
rows.B_note: Override, review, and agreement rates are measured and reported; effectiveness assessment is on cadence, but no evidence of independent validation or design revision from ineffectiveness.

rows.A_note: The dependency map (EV-340) and its quarterly review (EV-342) are good, but the open legal-review exceptions are not coverage. No coverage or reassessment metrics or closure-to-plan record is named for level 3.
rows.B_note: Systematic mapping and legal review are present for most, but not all, third-party AI; coverage fails for level 3.

rows.A_note: Independence is documented per engagement (EV-421 signed statement, EV-422 engagement letter), and EV-420 sets the audit scope. External assessors (a level 4 element) are present, but the level 3 coverage measure is absent, so the two-level rule holds the score at 2.
rows.B_note: External assessors engaged, independence documented, and programme changes traceable to findings

rows.A_note: EV-430 and EV-431 evidence manifests in version control with dataset hash, container digest, seed and metric code; EV-431 names the seed explicitly for 2026-08. rows.B_note: Reproducibility measured and reported, but no evidence of research-grade/public methodology or automation

rows.A_note: Multi-metric grouped analysis exists (EV-530), and the night-shift disparity was mitigated and retested (EV-531, EV-532). Per-release tracking against thresholds (EV-533) is a level 3 artefact, but level 2 fails first on the Brno disparity, so level 3 is not credited. EV-534 is a scoping decision about demographic analysis for VIC-2 and does not decide coverage for the other systems.
rows.B_note: Fairness tracked per group and release, but no intersectional analysis or public reporting

rows.A_note: Level 2 is met by EV-460, which covers all six systems. Level 3 has the metrics (precision 0.88, recall 0.83, alert-to-action median 3.5 h) and a named body (AI Steering Committee, quarterly), but no minutes prove a cadence. rows.B_note: Level 4 is satisfied: EV-463 records dated changes to alert thresholds from measured incident data, with before-and-after alert-to-action time, traceable to the motivating report (EV-462). Level-3 cadence and report are evidenced by EV-462.

rows.A_note: Withheld evidence is NA, not 0. EV-490 and EV-492 show the exercise exists but not its findings, resilience measures or retest dates. Absence was not established.
rows.B_note: EV-491 and EV-492 confirm the report is unavailable and no results or resilience measures are evidenced.

rows.A_note: EV-560 (owner, cadence) and EV-561 (9 of 9 months minuted) are strong. Under one artefact, one clause, per-system coverage cannot be inferred from the entry count, so the score is the level below.
rows.B_note: EV-560 and EV-561 evidence log, owner, cadence, and coverage, but no measurement of tracking coverage or time-to-log.

rows.A_note: The channel (EV-580: 210 items) and the feedback-to-change log (EV-582: 11 changes) are present. The pack does not address the appeal process, so its absence is not established and the score is NA rather than 0 or 1. Level 0 does not fit because a feedback route clearly exists.
rows.B_note: EV-580, EV-581, and EV-582 evidence channels, appeal process, and feedback-to-change linkage, but no measurement of volume, outcomes, or resolution times.

rows.A_note: EV-600 and EV-601 show independent validation, with the external lab's independence recorded and the Board's partial conflict noted and mitigated. EV-602 is a record of outcomes, not a measure.
rows.B_note: EV-600, EV-601, and EV-602 evidence independent review, coverage, and disagreement resolution, but not programme revision from external review.

rows.A_note: EV-610, EV-611 and EV-613 meet level 2: all 3 declines have a root cause, an action and a retest. rows.B_note: EV-610, EV-611, EV-612, and EV-613 evidence detection, root cause, action, and measured latency against targets, but not predictive modelling.
